executive_summary: April 8 was the single most consequential macro session of 2026. Pakistan brokered a last-minute US-Iran ceasefire hours before Trump's military deadline, triggering a 16% crude collapse and the sharpest single-day equity rally of the year. The mechanism is mechanical: WTI at $94 removes 3-4 months of energy-driven CPI pressure, re-opens the rate-cut optionality window, and delivers a direct cost windfall to every fuel-intensive business. DAL beat Q1 estimates and its Q2 guidance ($4.30/gal fuel) is now materially conservative — the most important earnings revision setup in airlines. The two-week clock started April 8; ceasefire expires ~April 22. Formal talks begin Friday in Islamabad. Iran's 10-point proposal (US withdrawal, sanction lifting) remains far from US stated positions — treat every day of ceasefire as borrowed time and keep stops tight on all ceasefire-driven longs.

macro_events.title: Pakistan-Brokered US-Iran Two-Week Ceasefire
macro_events.causal_chain: Pakistan PM Sharif and Army Chief Munir mediate → Trump suspends bombing campaign for 2 weeks → Iran Foreign Minister confirms Strait of Hormuz safe passage 'under Iranian military management' → WTI war risk premium collapses from $14/bbl to $4-6/bbl → WTI falls $117→$94.55 (-16.3%), Brent falls to $94.13 (-13.8%) → shipping rerouting costs reverse (Cape of Good Hope premium fades) → inflation trajectory reprices → Fed optionality improves → S&P +2.1%, QQQ +2.7%, RTY +3.6% → airlines, cruise, trucking, retail all re-rate → energy majors sell off
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East / Global shipping lanes / US-Iran bilateral
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack → recovery: Brent +15% in 24h then gave back over 3 weeks. Apr 2023 Saudi production cut: WTI +6% single day. But closest analog is May 2019 Hormuz tensions → oil spiked then immediately reversed when naval standoff deescalated.
macro_events.counterargument: Iran's formal 10-point proposal demands US full withdrawal and sanctions removal — positions the US has explicitly rejected. Attacks reportedly continued in early Wednesday hours even after ceasefire announcement. 'Neither side specified when the truce formally begins.' Shipping backlogs will take weeks to clear even if strait fully reopens.
